titulo: I have had my hair cut
intro: With me, te, le you say who something is done to. You do not need to name who does it.
p.pelo.consejo: «El pelo» is all the hair on the head. «Los pelos» are single hairs, one by one.
p.peluquería.consejo: It comes from «peluca». The person who works there is «el peluquero» or «la peluquera».
p.robar.consejo: The person who loses the thing goes with «le» or «me»: «le han robado la cartera».
p.cartera.consejo: The stress is on «TE»: kar-TE-ra. It is feminine: «la cartera».
p.arreglar.consejo: The rr is strong: a-rre-GLAR. It also means to tidy: «arreglar la habitación».
p.fontanero.consejo: It comes from «fuente». In several countries of the Americas people say «plomero».
p.grifo.consejo: In Spain it is «grifo»; in several countries of the Americas, «llave».
p.muela.consejo: It is feminine: «la muela». You say «me duele una muela» or «me han sacado una muela».
p.sacar.consejo: The c sounds like k before a: sa-KAR. In «saqué» it is written qu to keep that sound.
p.revisar.consejo: The v sounds like b: rre-bi-SAR. «Revisar el coche» means checking that it works.
p.manchar.consejo: It comes from «mancha». If it is done to you: «me han manchado la camisa».
p.camisa.consejo: The s is always voiceless: ka-MI-sa, never ka-MI-za. It is feminine.
b1.texto:
When another person does something to your body or to your things, the pronoun **me, te, le, nos, os, les** says who receives it.

- **Me han cortado** el pelo. (Someone has cut my hair.)
- **Le han robado** la cartera.
- **Te han arreglado** el grifo.

The verb is in the **ellos** form (han cortado, robaron, arreglaron) because it does not matter who did it. **Me he cortado el pelo** may mean you did it yourself; with **me han cortado**, someone else did.
b2.f0.texto: Have you had your hair cut?
b2.f1.texto: They have dyed it red at the hairdresser's.
b2.f2.texto: They have fixed the kitchen tap for me.
b2.f3.texto: I have had a tooth taken out this morning.
b2.f4.texto: And have you had your car checked?
b2.f5.texto: My brother had his bike stolen last night.
b2.f6.texto: Shall I make you a coffee?
b2.f7.texto: A coffee suits all of us very well.
b4.texto:
With the body, clothes and personal things, Spanish uses the **pronoun** and the **article**:

- **Me** han manchado **la** camisa. (not «mi camisa»)
- **Le** han robado **la** cartera.
- **Te** han sacado **una** muela.

The verb is in the third person plural (**han manchado**, **robaron**, **arreglaron**) when you do not know or do not care who did it.

To offer something to someone you use the same pronoun: ¿**Te hago** un café? ¿**Os llevo** las maletas?
b4.e0.texto: They have cut my hair very short.
b4.e2.texto: Have they fixed your tap yet?
b5.f0.texto: The hairdresser's on the corner smells of apple shampoo and magazine paper.
b5.f1.texto: The scissors sing beside Lucía's ear with a fine, bright sound.
b5.f2.texto: They cut her hair slowly, lock by lock, with calm hands.
b5.f3.texto: In the mirror a lighter face slowly appears.
b5.f4.texto: Lucía smiles when she sees it and runs her fingers through her new hair.
b5.f5.texto: At Pablo's house, the plumber works under the sink with a torch between his teeth.
b5.f6.texto: The old tap has been dripping for weeks with a heavy, monotonous rhythm.
b5.f7.texto: At last they fix the broken part for him with a small wrench.
b5.f8.texto: Pablo listens to the new silence of the kitchen and sighs with relief.
b5.f9.texto: Outside, a warm wind moves the curtains and brings the smell of freshly baked bread.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes! «Han cortado» leaves the subject unnamed: someone else did it.
b6.o1.refuerzo: If you had cut it yourself, you would say «me he cortado el pelo».
b6.o2.refuerzo: The hair is what gets cut, not who cuts it.
b6.pregunta: «Me han cortado el pelo». Who cut it?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done! With «me» the article is enough: the pronoun already says whose it is.
b7.o1.refuerzo: It repeats what «me» already says; Spanish uses the article.
b7.o2.refuerzo: Any shirt; here we are talking about yours.
b8.frase: A mi hermano le robaron la bici
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Me» would be for me: you are asking whether you make it for yourself.
b9.o1.refuerzo: That is it! «Te» is Lucía, who is going to receive it.
b9.o2.refuerzo: That question does not say who the coffee is for.
b9.pregunta: You are talking to Lucía. How do you offer her a coffee?
b10.frase: En el dentista me han sacado una ____.
b10.o0.refuerzo: A wallet is not in the mouth.
b10.o1.refuerzo: Nor is a shirt: the dentist works in the mouth.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Yes! A muela is a big tooth at the back of the mouth.
b10.pregunta: What do they take out of you at the dentist?
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «They stole my wallet».
b12.o0.refuerzo: No: «le» points to Lucía, who receives the change.
b12.o1.refuerzo: The hairdresser does it, but the hair is not his: it is Lucía's.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That is it! «A Lucía le» says whose hair it is.
b12.pregunta: «A Lucía le han teñido el pelo.» Whose hair is it?
p.teñido.consejo: Past participle of «teñir», for hair dye. «ñ» sounds like «ny», as in «ñandú», so say «te-NYI-do».
p.arreglado.consejo: Participle of «arreglar». In «¿Te han arreglado…?» it means someone repaired something for you.
p.revisado.consejo: Participle of «revisar», to check. In this lesson «¿…te han revisado el coche?» means has someone checked your car.
p.robaron.consejo: Past tense of «robar», to steal. Here «le robaron» means someone stole something from his brother.
p.tijeras.consejo: Always plural in Spanish: «las tijeras». The «j» sounds like «h».
p.cortan.consejo: Plural of «corta», from «cortar». «Le cortan el pelo» means they cut his or her hair.
p.mechón.consejo: A small group of hairs. The stress falls on the last syllable: «me-CHON».
p.verla.consejo: «Verla» means «to see her». The pronoun «la» is attached to the infinitive «ver».
p.fregadero.consejo: From «fregar», to scrub. The «g» before «a» sounds hard, like «g» in «gas».
p.gotea.consejo: From «gota», drop. The tap drips drop by drop. «Ea» is two separate syllables.
p.monótono.consejo: The accent on «ó» marks the stress: «mo-NO-to-no». Its root is «tono».
p.arreglan.consejo: Plural form of «arreglar». Here it means they repair the broken part.
p.pieza.consejo: In Spain «za» sounds like «th», so say «PYE-tha».
p.rota.consejo: Feminine of «roto», agreeing with «pieza». It starts with a strong «rr».
p.aliviado.consejo: Participle of «aliviar», to relieve. «Suspira aliviado» means he sighs with relief.
p.cortinas.consejo: Plural of «cortina». It is the fabric that hangs over a window.
p.manchado.consejo: Participle of «manchar». «Me han manchado» means someone stained my clothes.
p.dentista.consejo: Use «el dentista» for a man or a woman. The stress is on «TIS».
